chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: James Brown package tour and the Fillmore flop on Easter 1958
summary: Cobb leads the band on a California tour with James Brown and Little Willie John, plays to 200 people at the Fillmore, and has to wire Universal money to bail the band out of a hotel.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We left here in '58 going to California on a tour, and we played the Fillmore Auditorium in San Francisco on Easter Sunday with James Brown, Leslie Hawkins -- who is getting big now -- Arnett Cobb, band backing them up, and Little Willie Johns. And you could throw a brick in the place and it wouldn't hit nobody -- on Easter Sunday. Well, they had 200 people in there, but the place was big, and they're scattered, and you can't tell how many.
Well, he just started. He didn't have nothing out there. Oh, that's just the beginning I'm talking about.

And I've got the master contract, and I'm receiving the money and I'm paying everybody off. We leave there and we've got one nighters to do, and we're in San Francisco at the Booker T. Washington HOTEL and got the rainy roads to Royals worry about each day -- what about during the week, blocked off on account of flooded out.
I had to send to the office and get money to bail everybody out of the hotel. That's the truth. And I just couldn't take no more. That was my second trip to California from coast to coast.
